# The Evolution of Prince's Day in the Netherlands

## Summary

The September Declaration has a rough equivalent in the Netherlands, known as Prince's Day (Prinsjesdag), which takes place on the same day every year. This day marks the ceremonial opening of a new parliamentary year and is accompanied by a royal procession and the presentation of the national budget. The current name of this day, Prince's Day, has a rich history that dates back to the 18th century. This research brief aims to determine in which century the current name of Prince's Day was chosen. Through an analysis of historical sources, we will explore the origins of the name and its significance in the context of Dutch history and politics.

## Key Findings

* **The Name 'Prince's Day' Harks Back to the 18th Century**
The name Prince's Day (Prinsjesdag) has its roots in the 18th century, specifically during the time of Prince William V. According to the Government.nl website, the name harks back to the 18th century and the time of Prince William V, whose birthday (8 March) was known as Prince's Day. This suggests that the name was chosen in the 18th century, as a way to honor the prince and his legacy. The fact that the name has been retained to this day implies a strong sense of continuity and tradition in the Netherlands.

During the French occupation of the Netherlands, supporters of the House of Orange-Nassau demonstrated their loyalty to the prince by continuing to celebrate Prince's Day.
